test_title: PYST 39: RRB Group D - GA (Held On: 14 Dec, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: What is the maximum number of lenders allowed per borrower under new Microfinance Institutions Network (MFIN) rules which came into effect from 1 April 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Three**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Microfinance Institutions Network (MFIN)**, which is a **Self-Regulatory Organization (SRO)** for the microfinance sector, has introduced new guidelines to address concerns of **over-indebtedness** among borrowers.
 
• According to the updated rules, the maximum number of **Microfinance (MFI) lenders** allowed per borrower has been capped at **Three**.
 
• This new regulation is scheduled to come into full effect from **April 1, 2025**, providing a transition period for the industry to align its credit assessment processes.
 
• The decision was taken to ensure that borrowers do not enter a **debt trap** by borrowing from multiple sources, a practice often referred to as **loan stacking**.
 
• Under these rules, no lender should provide a loan to a borrower who already has active loans from **three** different microfinance institutions, regardless of the loan amount or the borrower's repayment capacity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Microfinance Institutions Network (MFIN):**
 
 
• Established in **2009**, **MFIN** is the premier industry association for the microfinance sector in India and is recognized by the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** as an **SRO**.
 
• Its primary role is to ensure **responsible lending** and ethical conduct among **Non-Banking Financial Company-Microfinance Institutions (NBFC-MFIs)**.
 
 
 
• **Microfinance Loan Definition:**
 
 
• As per the **RBI Master Directions (2022)**, a microfinance loan is a **collateral-free loan** given to a household having an annual income of up to **Rs. 3 lakh**.
 
• These loans are primarily aimed at **financial inclusion** for the unbanked and underbanked population.
 
 
 
• **Fixed Obligation to Income Ratio (FOIR):**
 
 
• Besides the lender limit, the **MFIN** rules emphasize that the **FOIR** should not exceed **50%**.
 
• This means that the total monthly loan repayment obligations of a household must not exceed **50%** of its **monthly income**.
 
 
 
• **Credit Information Companies (CICs):**
 
 
• Lenders are mandated to check the credit history of potential borrowers through **CICs** like **Equifax, Experian, or CIBIL** to verify the number of existing active lenders before sanctioning new credit.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Regulatory Harmony:** The **RBI** introduced a harmonized regulatory framework in **March 2022**, which removed the **interest rate cap** but shifted the focus toward a **risk-based pricing** model and **protection against over-leveraging**.
 
• **Implementation Timeline:** While the **SRO** issued these "guardrails" in late **2024**, the mandatory enforcement of the **three-lender limit** begins on the **1st of April, 2025**.
 
• **Industry Impact:** This move is expected to slow down **asset growth** for some aggressive lenders but will significantly improve the **asset quality** and sustainability of the microfinance ecosystem in the long run.
</ul
